subject: Kickoff: TideBank implementation — model shortlist, context and burst sizing
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Kickoff: TideBank implementation — model shortlist, context and burst sizing

Elena —

Great to meet yesterday. As promised, I pulled together an initial scope for the implementation kickoff so your engineers and product folks have visibility into the model/context tradeoffs we'll need to decide on during onboarding. Key asks in this note: confirm the three user flows below, validate the peak QPS assumptions, and land on a target API SLA (p95 latency) so we can pick the right model tier and caching strategy.

High-level: TideBank wants a pilot for contextual transaction summarization and policy-aware response generation inside the banking portal. We typically evaluate 3 candidate model tiers during pilot (cost/perf tradeoffs):
- Small context specialized (up to 1k tokens) — lower cost, fast latency for single-turn summaries.
- Medium context (2–4k tokens) — reasonable latency, supports short threads and metadata.
- Long-window (8k+) — supports multi-message conversation state and larger KV caching footprint.

Flows to confirm (please reply inline):
1) Transaction summarization: single-user request + 1–2 prior messages (expected avg prompt 600 tokens, avg completion 150 tokens).
2) Dispute triage assistant: requires 2–6 messages of history and up to 2k prompt tokens, completion up to 400 tokens.
3) Regulatory redaction check: large document extraction from attachments, expect occasional spikes (one-off) up to 6k prompt tokens.

Estimated steady-state token volume (initial pilot assumptions) — please confirm if these are close to your telemetry:
- Active users (pilot): 2,500/day
- Avg requests per user/day: 3
- Avg prompt tokens/request: 900
- Avg completion tokens: 200
=> Daily tokens ~= (900+200) * 2,500 * 3 = ~7.875M tokens/day
Peak burst planning: we should plan for 6x steady-state bursts during payroll/statement cycles.

Attachments: tidebank_mvp_token_estimates.xlsx (xlsx) — I attached a quick workbook with per-flow token bands and a cost burn estimate across model tiers.

Next steps I recommend:
- Your confirmation of flows + any adjustments to token assumptions by EOD Thu.
- Quick 45m tech kickoff with your infra and security folks — propose Thu 12/3 11:00 PT.
- Marcus will draft an initial shortlist with quantization/latency expectations.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Monica

Elena/Monica/Grace —

Thanks for the confirmation, Elena. I pulled a short technical note and attached a workbook that breaks out token volume per flow, expected latency bands, and a recommended shortlist. Summary below (high level):

Model shortlist (initial pilot):
- opt-imx-3b-4k (small-medium): lowest-cost candidate, good for transaction summaries (p95 ~120–160ms token path on our Dedicated nodes), recommended with prefix caching for repeated templates.
- lla-mini-7b-8k (medium): balances context vs latency; expect p95 generation latency ~200–260ms on standard Dedicated profile. Good for dispute triage with 2–4 messages.
- redwood-xl-30b-16k (long-window): supports the regulatory/redaction flow without truncation; higher memory and cost, recommend for asynchronous redaction jobs (batching) rather than synchronous UI calls.

Caching and retention note:
- Prefix/KV caching can reduce prompt token cost by 25–45% for repeated metadata (templates, common instruction blocks). Redwood's default caching scrubs ephemeral session keys; PII should not be persisted in long-lived caches unless explicitly configured.
- For regulatory flows, recommend processing large attachments in a private VPC deployment or dedicated batch pipeline to avoid injecting large document text into low-cache serving tiers.

Sizing highlights (pilot = 1,000 active users/day, 3 requests/user):
- Steady-state daily tokens ~= (900+200)*1,000*3 = ~3.3M tokens/day.
- Peak burst factor (your telemetry): 5x => short window throughput target ~16.5M tokens/day equivalent, or sustained ~192 tokens/sec average during 24h but bursts concentrated in 30m windows => we convert to QPS: assume avg request ~1100 tokens => burst QPS ~ (16.5M / 1800s) = ~9,200 tokens/s -> at 1.3k tokens/request ≈ 7 QPS of full requests, but note token-per-second compute differs by model.

Operational recs:
- Start pilot on lla-mini-7b-8k for the UI flows; route redwood-xl-16k for batch redaction jobs only.
- Configure a 1-hour canary of traffic through quantized (int8) variants for cost comparison.
- Implement automatic fallback to smaller model (opt-imx-3b-4k) when latency SLO breaches 2x baseline.

Attachments: model_shortlist_notes.pdf (pdf), tidebank_mvp_token_estimates.xlsx (xlsx). Detailed per-flow sheets in the workbook include hourly token-band scenarios and a simple autoscaling knob map.

I can be on the call Thu to walk the infra folks through the latency and cache tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
